clauses.reason: Executive Order 7759 consists of two recitals and one command: Executive Orders No. 7024-B (April 25, 1935) and No. 7129-A (August 6, 1935) are revoked and superseded by Executive Order No. 7757 and Executive Order No. 7758. The text contains no deferred effective date, no condition, no duration, no continuing duty and no direction to any officer to do anything later. The revocation is self-executing and was complete when the order was approved on December 1, 1937 (signed by Harold L. Ickes, Secretary of the Interior, and approved by President Franklin D. Roosevelt on the date the order prints, Dec. 1, 1937). The Federal Register published it at 2 FR 3097 in the issue of December 4, 1937; the alternative reading that the revocation took effect on filing or publication would give a date a few days later, but no wording in the held text defers the revocation to filing or publication. The first end is therefore the approval date of December 1, 1937, by performance of the order's own command (mechanism: spent on issue). No later instrument is needed for the end, and nothing can end the clause earlier than its own approval.

research_rationale:
EO 7759 (Revoking Executive Orders Nos. 7024-B and 7129-A; 2 FR 3097; approved Dec. 1, 1937) was read in full from the held Federal Register original. It is a single self-executing revocation of two earlier petroleum-shipment orders, so its one clause was exhausted on issue and the whole order is not in force on 2026-10-14. Status review: the order has no provisional status in the ledger; the status decision file for this member records the proposal 'no' on the order's own terms, and its one catalog observation (Revokes: EO 7024-B; EO 7129-A) concerns the targets, not this order. The held Office of the Federal Register note on EO 7759 lists Revokes: EO 7024-B and EO 7129-A, and See: EO 6979, EO 6980-C, EO 7757 and EO 7758; none of these entries says this order was amended, revoked or superseded, and the bounded searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Federal Register catalog and saved order texts) found no later instrument that acts on EO 7759.

The order revokes two named orders and names the two orders that replace them; it creates no new duty, authority, deadline or exception of its own.","savings_check":"See the savings field: the revocation is an accrued result and the functions pass to EO 7757 and EO 7758, both of which the order names; no pending-matter saving clause is stated.","scope_check":"The dossier inventory is one clause, 'whole', covering the sole operative paragraph. I read the held original text and confirm that it holds no other operative sentence: the two WHEREAS recitals describe EO 7024-B and EO 7129-A, and the NOW, THEREFORE paragraph is the only command."}

savings.reason: The order itself says the two revoked orders are superseded by Executive Order No. 7757 (Regulations Under the Act of February 22, 1935 As Amended by the Act of June 14, 1937) and Executive Order No. 7758 (Constituting Designated Area, and Establishing Federal Tender Board No. 1); the functions of the revoked orders were carried by those two orders and the revocation stands as an accrued result. The text of EO 7759 contains no savings clause for pending matters, so none is claimed beyond that transfer.
